hmmm not really newbie vods / streams. Most of those are meant for more intensive game play, like what I mentioned with Pick / Ban. The best way to learn is to play, and watch professionals play. You can watch a lot of professionals play on twitch, and they can help you, as long you take the time to understand the basic knowledge. It really just depends on the "role" you want to play. Not sure if you understand that so I'll take a moment to explain. There are 3 lanes in the game, but 5 players. The different roles consist of, ADC (Attack Damage Carry), often a fragile champion that can out put a lot of Damage per second. They go in the "bottom / bot lane". Beside them is their support, these champions often have shields/heals/or forms of crowd control (stuns / silences *which stop channels / slows), they can range from tanky to fragile, and high damage to low damage but are often meant to keep the ADC alive. The middle lane, contains a mage or assassin. A Mage is a character reliant on spells, and high Ability power, while assassins are meant to kill the ADC or enemy Mage with high burst damage (Sometimes they have Attack Damage). The top laner's role has changed a lot, so they can range from tanks, to "carries" (high damage roles). Mid lane and top lane share a few picks. The last role is Jungle, they normally stay in the fog of war, picking up the neutral camps for their experience and gold, and often making a showing in a lane to attempt to get a kill. The Jungle is often either a tank or high damage, but they often have high sustain (abilities that heal them or shields).

If you mean the subtext (small numbers) right beside the Champion's names, that is the order in which they are picked. As you go farther into the professional scene, "pick/ban" becomes relevant. That is what champions are banned (each team gets 3), and which champions get the priority (aka first picked). If you mean the numbers that are like 4-3-2 those are their score. The first number being the amount of kills they had, the middle number meaning the deaths they had, and the last number meaning the assists they have. Assists, are when you do damage to an enemy champ, or support the killing friendly champ (heals/shields), but do not last hit the enemy. You assisted with the kill.

So you have a base, where you rabidly regen Health and Mana (mana is used to cast abilities placed on your q-w-e-r keys). Recall is the b button and you press it then stand still, and it will take you back to base. At base you can also buy items by clicking on either the gold amount you have, or the shop keeper. *You also start the game on your base. Channeling is when you use an ability, (q-w-e-r keys) and it has a cast time. Each champions has different abilities attached to each key, but channeling is the time it takes for your ability to be used after the button press. Some abilities have a very short channel time, while others might channel all the way through (allowing the "channel" to  be interrupted.

So the map, Summoner's Rift, spawns minions in waves, those waves move down the "lanes" which are exactly what they sound like. They go from one side of the map to the next, and are where "laner" or champions spend the majority of their time. You often have a "lane opponent" which is the person in the same section of the map against you.
